    About NYC property tax

    Modeled billed residential property tax for FY2024 (July 2023–June 2024), not observed payments by race. Includes owner-occupied, additional and rented housing selected as directly owned by individuals.

    Likely LLCs, trusts, corporations and estates are excluded using owner-name indicators; this does not verify legal ownership. Co-ops and condops are excluded. The pool is reconstructed from final taxable assessments, tax rates, residential floor-area shares where available, and property-type abatement ratios.

    Group shares are a scenario allocation using ACS homeowner counts × median home values. The same proxy is applied to rentals and additional homes; actual landlord ethnicity is not observed. ACS owner counts also include co-op households, and small groups are especially uncertain. Figures are rounded to millions and sum to $6,713 million.

    NYC FY2024 tax report ↗ · Property assessment data ↗

    Federal tax is modeled from mean household income: Single, $14,600 standard deduction, no tax credits.

    Income and wealth are household aggregates. Per-person figures divide them by the group's residents; groups follow the householder's classification, so per-person values are approximate.

    Sources & methodology

    About the data

    The atlas uses the prepared 2024 dataset. The map and state rankings cover 50 states. The United States overview combines all 50 states and the District of Columbia. The city ranking currently contains New York City.

    Per-person figures

    “Per person” divides each amount by the resident population of the same area or group (ACS B03002). For groups, income, net worth and tax are classified by the householder, while population counts every resident, so group per-person values are an approximation: mixed households are attributed to the householder's group. Comparisons “vs US” use the national total divided by the national population, including DC. Corporate tax per person uses state population, although collections are assigned by a company's principal office.

    Population

    ACS 2024 1-Year, table B03002. Hispanic / Latino includes any race; all other groups exclude Hispanic people. State population totals come from ACS. In a few states, component estimates differ from the total by one person.

    Household income

    Aggregate annual household income in 2024 dollars. White non-Hispanic and Hispanic use B19025H/I. Other non-Hispanic groups are modeled using race-level income and population composition, calibrated to each state's income total. Household groups follow the householder's classification.

    Net worth

    All state and detailed group values are preliminary modeled estimates, not official state wealth statistics. Federal Reserve DFA national wealth at the end of 2024 is allocated using housing values, household counts and income, net of debt. DFA's Other category is split into five groups. Values are rounded to the nearest million dollars. National net worth includes DC and reconciles to the four DFA category totals.

    The model does not directly observe concentrations of stock ownership, private businesses or very wealthy families. ACS and DFA classifications are not identical. Reconciliation checks arithmetic, not accuracy.

    Federal income tax

    This is a mean-income model, not actual taxes paid. Mean household income equals aggregate income divided by household count. Each household is treated as one Single filer with a $14,600 standard deduction, ordinary-income tax brackets for 2024, and no tax credits. Tax on the mean income is multiplied by the number of households. State totals sum eight groups; the national total sums the state and DC calculations, rather than recalculating tax on a national mean.

    White non-Hispanic and Hispanic household counts come from ACS B25003H/I. Other groups use B25006 counts adjusted by non-Hispanic population shares. The model excludes itemized and additional deductions, preferential capital-gains rates, AMT, NIIT, payroll and self-employment taxes. A household may include multiple tax returns, and tax on mean income is not mean actual tax under progressive rates. Vermont's modeled zero Pacific Islander household count produces zero modeled tax.

    Federal corporate income tax

    IRS Data Book 2024, Table 5, Business income taxes column. Gross collections before refunds, including penalties and interest, for federal fiscal year 2024 (October 2023–September 2024). This published category combines corporation income tax (Form 1120 series) with unrelated business income tax from tax-exempt organizations (Form 990-T); the state table does not separate them.

    States are assigned by the principal office or place of business, not where all operations or profits occur. These are federal collections, not state-government corporate taxes. The national figure is the IRS United States total ($565,085,519,000), including DC, territories, international and undistributed collections, so it exceeds the displayed 50-state sum. No race or ethnicity allocation is made. NYC is not separately available.

    IRS 2024 collections by state — source table ↗

    New York City

    NYC population and aggregate household income use ACS 2024 1-Year tables B03002 and B19025. The same non-Hispanic allocation and 2024 federal tax model used for states are applied to the city. Total household net worth is the supplied $5.31 trillion estimate for 2026 Q1. White, Black and Hispanic wealth follow the supplied category estimates; the Other pool is split into the atlas groups using the supplied 2022 SCF Asian-versus-other wealth relationship and ACS household composition. The eight displayed amounts reconcile exactly to $5.31 trillion. NYC is not added to New York State or national totals.

    National scope and sorting

    National population and income are sums of state and DC values from the same dataset; modeled group results are aggregated consistently. They are not separately sourced national CPS estimates. State rankings use each state's overall totals (or per-person values) and exclude DC.

    Reading the map

    Largest group means the most numerous group, even below 50%. In metric mode, color intensity runs linearly from the lowest to the highest state value shown on the scale. Income and tax are annual flows; net worth is a year-end stock.
